local_patches.summary: v5.5/v5.6 field fixes (#414) applied to the vendored bundle in place, pending upstreaming — the shipped tableau.mjs is source_commit plus the changes below.
changes: multi-datasource merge: dedupe merged controls by controlId before display name — two child datasources can emit controls with different names but the same param-derived controlId, which the name-only key let through and the DM POST rejected as duplicate ids

multi-datasource merge: child conversions (options.__multiDsChild) no longer call resetIds() — children continue the monotonic element-id counter so the merged dm-spec stays duplicate-free; top-level single-datasource conversions keep the reset for corpus id determinism

no default warehouse db/schema: new warehouseDbSchemaFromConn() derives database/schema from the workbook's own warehouse <connection> attrs (non-warehouse classes and file-path/.hyper dbnames skipped) when no --database/--schema override is passed; the root relation and each side of a blend fall back to their own connection instead of a fabricated default

calc flexibility: federated-join cross-table coalesce synthesis — IFNULL/ZN/IF-ISNULL cross-table fallback calcs are rewritten to Coalesce(local, Lookup(target column, join keys)); join-key collection walks AND-wrapped equality clauses so every key pair is kept (leftKeys/rightKeys), not just the first top-level '='
calc flexibility: bare-ref case-fold — case- and underscore-normalized display-name indexes so bare column references resolve across tables regardless of casing

calc flexibility: parameter member aliases captured (memberAliases value->alias) and emitted as the manual-list control's labels[] — values stay the codes translated calcs compare against; labels only change the rendered option text
comment-only hygiene neutralization of a workbook name in the multi-datasource comment (no behavior change)

local_patches.commit: worktree (uncommitted at patch time — becomes the landing commit of the PR #508 calc-hotfix batch)
local_patches.summary: Calc-translation hotfixes (PR #508 speed-program batch, live-verified bugs) applied to the vendored bundle in place AND to the local vendor source tree (scripts/vendor/sigma-data-model-mcp src/formulas.ts + rebuilt build/ + updated src tests), pending upstreaming. Fallback path used deliberately: the local upstream clone does not contain source_commit d769bec (divergent history, dirty src/tableau.ts) and re-bundling from any source tree would drop the unlanded d8a049a bundle-only patches above.
changes: ZN → native Sigma Zn() via TABLEAU_FUNC_MAP name-map; removed the single-paren Coalesce($1, 0) regex that emitted malformed Coalesce(Sum([x], 0)) for ZN(AGG(...)) — the dominant field null-guard idiom

removed Coalesce from _TEXT_FN_RE: its type follows its args, and counting it as text-producing turned numeric ZN(a)+ZN(b) addition into silent string concat (&); _isTextOperand instead recurses into Coalesce's top-level args, so string-literal guard chains (Coalesce([a], "x") + …) still convert + to & while numeric or unknown-type guards keep +

start-of-week literal handling: DATETRUNC 3rd arg / 4-arg DATEDIFF 'monday' is still dropped (Sigma has no start-of-week slot) but now emits a verify warning instead of silent week-boundary drift; the drop is scoped to DateTrunc/DateDiff via a balanced-paren walk so other calls keeping a weekday string as a real last argument (e.g. CONTAINS(x, 'monday')) are no longer mangled

stopped emitting non-existent Sigma functions: DATETIME → Date (was Datetime), DATEPART('weekday'/'dayofweek') → Weekday(date) with a numbering-verify warning (was DayOfWeek), DATENAME('week') → Text(DatePart("week", …)) at the source branch (was Text(Week(…)))

un-staled the window-untranslatable list: WINDOW_CORR/WINDOW_VAR/WINDOW_COUNT now map to MovingCorr/MovingVariance/MovingCount (offset forms spanning the current row; all three present in the Sigma function index, verified 2026-07-25); population variants WINDOW_VARP/COVARP/STDEVP stay untranslatable; SIGMA_CHART_ONLY_WINDOW_RE extended with MovingVariance/MovingCorr so the DM router keeps refusing them

local_patches.summary: Object-graph relationship key derivation ladder + coverage ledger (PR2a, bead beads-sigma-ovy4): Tableau's 2020.2+ logical model auto-matches relationships by column name at query time and serializes no join key, so the converter previously saw a modern star schema and emitted disconnected tables — after which a parity gate with no relationships to satisfy it pushed the run into joined/aggregated Custom SQL. Applied in place per the standing PROVENANCE TASK 3 guard: two prior local_patches entries above are still open/unlanded, and re-vendoring would silently drop them.
changes: object-graph relationship loop (relType === "collection"): the auto-match branch (previously an unconditional `continue` when the relationship carried zero serialized equality expressions) now first attempts conservative name-match inference — candidate column names are the normalized (whitespace-to-underscore, uppercased) display names already present on BOTH elements' colIdMap (existence tested via ensureCol's own bare lookup, never via a mutating call), filtered to key-shaped names by isKeyShapedName (see the dedicated bullet below for its exact, review-tightened rule). A single key-shaped candidate is wired with derivedVia: "name-inference"; ensureCol is only ever called on a name already confirmed to exist on both sides, so inference can fabricate neither a column nor a value. More than one key-shaped candidate, or none, leaves the relationship unwired — never a guessed composite key

entityNameOf(cleanName) — the 'target element's entity name' used by the key-shaped filter above: uppercases the target element's cleanName, then strips exactly one leading prefix matching /^(DIM|FACT|BRIDGE)_/ (so 'DIM_CUSTOMER' -> 'CUSTOMER', 'FACT_WIDE' -> 'WIDE', 'BRIDGE_ACCOUNT_USER' -> 'ACCOUNT_USER'; a cleanName with none of those three prefixes, e.g. 'CUSTOMER', passes through unchanged). The prefix match is effectively case-insensitive end-to-end because cleanName is uppercased before the regex runs (so 'dim_customer' or 'Dim_Customer' both strip to 'CUSTOMER' too) — only that single fixed 3-name prefix list is recognized; any other table-naming convention (no prefix, or a prefix outside DIM/FACT/BRIDGE) falls back to matching the full cleanName as the entity name, which may under-match the _ID/_KEY/_SK/_CODE suffix leg's sibling checks on real-world schemas that use different prefixing

REVIEW FIX (2026-07-30, Critical/Important findings 2+3): isKeyShapedName originally used `name.includes(entityName)` for the entity-name leg, which was both too loose and too strict in exactly the ways spike risk 2 warned about. Reproduced wrong-wire: a fact carrying a denormalized CUSTOMER_NAME whose real key (CUST_KEY) doesn't name-match the dim's real key (CUSTOMER_KEY) left CUSTOMER_NAME as the only shared candidate, and `includes` counted it as key-shaped ("CUSTOMER_NAME".includes("CUSTOMER")) — silently wiring the join on a name column a dimension is typically unique on, which gate 16's uniqueness probe cannot catch (a wrong-but-unique key sails through). Reproduced wrong-discard: ORDER_DATE contains "DATE", so a fact/DIM_DATE pair sharing both DATE_KEY and ORDER_DATE saw 2 candidates counted key-shaped under `includes` and refused to wire the obvious DATE_KEY as "ambiguous" — an unwired star is exactly the condition this PR exists to prevent. Fixed: isKeyShapedName(name, entityName) is now `/_(ID|KEY|SK|CODE)$/.test(name) || !!entityName && (name === entityName || new RegExp('^' + escapeRe(entityName) + '_(ID|KEY|SK|CODE)$').test(name))` — three precise forms only: an explicit key suffix (entity-agnostic: two unrelated *_ID columns shared between two tables still correctly yield 2 candidates and no guess, by design), the entity name exactly, or the entity name plus a key suffix. A new escapeRe(s) helper (regex-metacharacter escaping) guards the third form so an entity name is never interpolated into a RegExp unescaped. Verified against all four scenarios: CUSTOMER_NAME no longer qualifies, CUST_KEY and CUSTOMER_KEY both qualify (via the suffix leg and the entity+suffix leg respectively), ORDER_DATE no longer qualifies, DATE_KEY still qualifies

computed-only key branch (all serialized equality expressions resolved to non-physical/computed operands, previously an unconditional `continue`): now attempts the same name-match inference before giving up, so a relationship with no serializable physical key can still be recovered by name when the columns exist on both sides

mixed-key branch (skippedComputed > 0, some equality expressions computed and dropped alongside a wired physical subset): unchanged wiring behavior, now additionally tags the relationship and its coverage-ledger entry with derivedVia: "serialized", partial: true, droppedConditions: <n>
every relationship object pushed into an element's `relationships` array now carries derivedVia: "serialized" | "name-inference"

new relationshipCoverage ledger: a `{ serialized, wired, entries: [] }` collector initialized before the relationship loop, attached to convertTableauToSigma's returned object as `relationshipCoverage` whenever the collection/object-graph branch runs. Every relationship the loop considers — wired or not — pushes exactly one entry (`{ left, right, derivedVia, keyCount }` when wired, or `{ left, right, derivedVia: "unwired", reason, candidates }` when not), so a relationship can never be silently absent from coverage the way it previously could be silently `continue`d out of the loop

REVIEW FIX (2026-07-30, Important finding 4): two early `continue` paths in the per-relationship loop — missing first-end-point/second-end-point elements, and endpoint object-id(s) that don't resolve to a known element (including both endpoints resolving to the SAME element, e.g. a malformed self-referencing relationship) — previously exited without pushing any coverage-ledger entry at all, so relationshipCoverage.entries could be shorter than relationshipCoverage.serialized with no record of why. Reproduced: a 3-relationship fixture with one unresolvable second-end-point object-id gave serialized: 3 but entries.length: 2 before the fix. Both paths now push a derivedVia: "unwired" entry with a reason naming the actual cause ("relationship XML is missing a first-end-point or second-end-point", "endpoint object-id unresolved to a known element (first=..., second=...)", or "both endpoints resolve to the same element"), using the raw object-id string as left/right when no element resolved enough to supply a cleanName

REVIEW FIX (2026-07-30, fix-wave on this same PR, Important finding 2): the computed-only branch's successful-inference path (keys.length === 0, inferRelationshipKeyByName().ok) called wireInferred(name) with no way to record that skippedComputed conditions had been dropped — when EVERY serialized condition on a relationship was computed (e.g. IFNULL(...) = [KEY]) and name-inference then found a key-shaped column shared on both sides, the relationship wired cleanly as derivedVia: "name-inference" with no partial/droppedConditions on either the relationship object or its coverage-ledger entry, and the skippedComputed warning was never reached (the branch continues before it). The resulting join is strictly WIDER than Tableau's (the dropped computed condition no longer narrows matches) but looked exactly like the auto-matched no-conditions-at-all case (FACT_WIDE->DIM_CUSTOMER) in every artifact — the mixed-key serialized branch already flagged the analogous case (partial: true, droppedConditions: <n>, a dropped-condition warning) but computed-only-then-inferred did not. Fixed: wireInferred(name, { droppedConditions }) now accepts the skipped-computed count and, when positive, spreads partial: true, droppedConditions: <n> onto BOTH the pushed relationship object and the coverage-ledger entry (same shape the mixed-key/serialized branch already used) and pushes an additional ⚠ warning naming the join as wider than Tableau's. The computed-only call site now passes { droppedConditions: skippedComputed }; the eqExprs.length === 0 (no serialized condition at all) call site is unaffected (nothing was dropped there — it never had a condition to drop). Regression-covered by corpus/tableau/logical-model-objectgraph's 4th relationship (FACT_WIDE->DIM_STORE, added this fix-wave: IFNULL([STORE_KEY],-1) = [STORE_KEY], the only fixture case where inference succeeds AND a computed condition was dropped) and two new assertions in test-relationship-derivation.rb.

KNOWN LIMITATION, NOT FIXED THIS ROUND (spike risk 1, Minor finding 5): hasCol/candidateNames trust colIdMap, and every write into colIdMap (both the metaCols and fallback column-build loops, and ensureCol's own writes) is a bare assignment with no existence check — if two distinct physical columns on the SAME element normalize to the same key (e.g. captions "Order-ID" and "Order_ID" colliding under whitespace-only normalization), the later write silently wins and name-inference could resolve to a real-but-WRONG column's id with no signal a collision occurred. This is a correctness risk distinct from fabrication (hasCol still only ever returns a real, existing id) and is deliberately left unmitigated pending a follow-up that would need to change colIdMap's write sites themselves, not just the relationship loop that reads it

all pre-existing warnings.push(...) message text is unchanged and verbatim for every branch where the original condition (still, or now-additionally, unwired) still holds; new ℹ info-level warnings.push messages were added only for the newly-successful name-inference wire paths, explicitly calling out that the key was inferred (not serialized) and should be verified

_upstream_and_revendor_tasks: Standing vendoring rule: patch upstream and re-vendor; never edit the vendored .mjs in place. When an in-place patch is unavoidable, it lands with its own local_patches entry (commit, summary, upstream_pr) in this file — the hygiene.yml converter-provenance guard rejects any plugins/**/converter/*.mjs diff whose range does not also change the sibling PROVENANCE.json.
TASK 1 — upstream: port each open local_patches entry to source_repo's tableau converter source, one reviewable PR per functional change; set the entry's upstream_pr field when the PR opens.

TASK 2 — re-vendor: after the upstream PR merges, run tools/vendor-converters.sh <checkout> tableau; the source_commit/source_commit_date bump and regeneration of this file are what retire landed local_patches entries.

TASK 3 — guard the unlanded: BOTH regenerators rewrite this file wholesale — tools/vendor-converters.sh (the canonical path) AND the skill-local scripts/dev/vendor-converter.sh (whose header still says to re-run it after converter changes, and which writes a stale schema with no local_patches at all) — so regenerating while any local_patches entry is still open silently drops that patch record; either wait, or re-apply the patch and re-record local_patches (and this task block) in the same commit. Refresh only via tools/vendor-converters.sh.
TASK 4 — prove parity: after any re-vendor, corpus/run-corpus.sh --check and corpus/converter-default-test.sh must stay green before a retirement counts as done.
